```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 18_regression_first_guess
title: Make a guess
questions:
  - id: unknown_coffee
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Say we don't know how much coffee the new student drank. What test score would you guess they
      will get?
    answer: 70
    tolerance: 0
    hint: >
      The horizontal dashed line marks the mean test score. Use the
      vertical scale to read it.
    explanation: >
      Knowing nothing about the student's coffee consumption, the average test score, 70, is a reasonable guess. Lacking any additional information, we have no reason to expect them to be anything other than
      average on the test.

  - id: average_coffee
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Now suppose the new student tells you they drank exactly one cup of coffee, the
      average amount for our sample so far. What score would you guess they
      will get?
    answer: 70
    tolerance: 0
    hint: >
      The horizontal dashed line marks the mean test score. Use the
      vertical scale to read it.
    explanation: >
      Knowing the student drank the average amount of coffee, the average test score, 70, is still the most reasonable guess. If someone is average on
      coffee, we have no reason to expect them to be anything other than
      average on the test.

  - id: more_coffee
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Now say they drank a cup and a half, more than average. Would you change your guess?
    options:
      - text: I'd guess higher
      - text: I'd guess lower
        correct: true
      - text: I would not change my guess
    explanation: >
      The correlation was negative: students who drank more coffee than
      average tended to score below average. So we'd guess lower than 70. But
      how much lower? The correlation on its own can't tell us that.

  - id: precise_guess
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    answerLabel: Example answer
    prompt: >
      What exact score would you predict for a student
      who drank a cup and a half? What about a student who drank no coffee? How did you decide?
    answer: >
      There's no single right answer yet. But you probably looked at the
      students around a cup and a half and picked a score that's typical for
      them. Do that for every amount of coffee and you'd be tracing a path
      through the middle of the points.
```
